correctness.rationale: For squarefree m, sigma(m^2) factors as a product of q^2+q+1. If p and q are distinct support primes congruent to 2 modulo 3 and p divides q^2+q+1, then q would give a nontrivial cube root of unity modulo p; this is impossible because 3 does not divide p-1, with p=2 checked separately. Thus gcd(m,sigma(m^2))=1. The Dirichlet series of the family has the exact factorization F(s)^2=(zeta(s)/L(s,chi_3))(1-3^(-s)) product_{p=2 mod 3}(1-p^(-2s)); the remaining factor is analytic and nonzero at 1. Selberg--Delange with exponent 1/2 gives the stated asymptotic and constant. The packaged checker independently confirms the local conclusion for every family member through 10^5 and the counting regression through 10^6.
